issues.t: 10-speed transmission damage can lock the wheels (recall)
issues.sym: Hard or jerky shifts, a shudder, or in the worst cases the wheels suddenly locking or the car losing drive at highway speed, often with no warning light.
issues.why: Parts inside the 10-speed automatic used in 2019-2020 CT6 models can break. GM recalled these cars (NHTSA 25V148000) to add software that watches for the damage and protects the driver.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and book the free update. If the car shifts harshly or shudders, have it checked before more highway driving; if the wheels lock, steer to the shoulder and have it towed.

issues.t: Harsh shifts and shudder from a cracked 10-speed valve body
issues.sym: The car slams into gear, jerks, shudders at various speeds, or seems to slip, sometimes without a check engine light.
issues.why: Owners report dealers finding a fractured transmission control valve body (the part that routes fluid to shift the gears). Several had to wait for parts or a full transmission replacement.
issues.next: Ask a Cadillac dealer to read transmission codes and check the valve body, and ask whether repairs are covered by the recall or the powertrain warranty. Keep records of every visit.

issues.t: Rough shifting, hesitation or slipping from the 8-speed automatic
issues.sym: Harsh shifts from park to reverse or between gears, a delay before the car moves from a stop, slipping, surging, or a lurch when the engine restarts after auto stop.
issues.why: The 8-speed automatic in early CT6 models is the most complained-about part of the car. Causes reported by owners include worn-out fluid, software, wiring harness faults and, in some cases, a failed torque converter.
issues.next: Have the transmission fluid and software checked first, as GM has updated both. If the problem keeps returning, ask for a full diagnosis of the torque converter and transmission before the warranty runs out.

issues.t: Shudder at light throttle from the 8-speed automatic
issues.sym: A shake or shudder, like driving over rumble strips, when accelerating gently at moderate speeds.
issues.why: The original transmission fluid in the 8-speed automatic can cause the torque converter to shudder. GM issued bulletins telling dealers to flush the old fluid and refill with a newer fluid.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about GM bulletin 18-NA-355 and the related transmission fluid coverage. The fluid change usually cures it if done before the converter is damaged.

issues.t: Loss of power, stalling or reduced engine power
issues.sym: The car suddenly loses power to the wheels, jerks, stalls, or shows a check engine light with a reduced power warning, sometimes at highway speed.
issues.why: Owners report repeated visits for reduced power and stalling. Causes found range from turbo boost faults to transmission and wiring problems, and some cars needed several repair attempts.
issues.next: If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Have codes read right away and keep repair records in case the problem repeats.

issues.t: Front passenger seat belt anchor bolt may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing. The front passenger belt could come loose from its anchor in a crash.
issues.why: A small number of 2016 CT6 cars built in July 2016 may have been assembled without the bolt that holds the passenger belt webbing to its anchor plate (NHTSA 16V687000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer installs the bolt for free.

issues.t: Child seat anchors blocked by excess adhesive (recall)
issues.sym: It is hard or impossible to clip a child seat onto the lower anchors in the back seat.
issues.why: Extra structural glue was left on the inboard child seat anchor bars at the factory, so a child seat may not latch properly (NHTSA 18V437000).
issues.next: Check for open recalls before installing a child seat. A dealer cleans off the glue and treats the bars for free.

issues.t: Rear seat belts may not lock to hold a child seat (recall)
issues.sym: A rear seat belt pulled all the way out does not switch into its locking mode, so a child seat held by the belt may stay loose.
issues.why: Some rear seat belt retractors may not lock when fully extended (NHTSA 18V673000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer inspects the retractors and replaces them if needed, free.

issues.t: Stability control and ABS can switch off without warning (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptom until you need it: the anti-lock brakes and stability control may not work, and the dash warning light may not come on.
issues.why: A software error in the electronic brake control module can disable ABS and stability control (NHTSA 19V889000).
issues.next: Check for open recalls. A dealer reprograms the brake module for free.

issues.sym: The front parking or position lights look unusually bright and can dazzle other drivers.
issues.why: The park and position lamps on these cars put out more light than the federal standard allows (NHTSA 21V759000).
issues.next: Check for open recalls. A dealer adds small wiring jumpers to both headlights for free.

issues.t: Turn signal does not cancel after a turn (recall)
issues.sym: The turn signal keeps blinking after you straighten the wheel.
issues.why: A faulty turn signal switch on a handful of 2019 cars does not cancel the signal (NHTSA 19V117000).
issues.next: Check for open recalls; the dealer replaces the switch for free.

issues.t: Tire pressure warning may not work with dealer-installed 20-inch wheels (recall)
issues.sym: The low tire pressure light does not come on even when a tire is low.
issues.why: Some 2020 CT6s fitted with dealer accessory 20-inch wheels got tire pressure sensors that use the wrong radio frequency (NHTSA 19V731000).
issues.next: Check tire pressures with a gauge and check for open recalls. A dealer replaces all four sensors for free.

issues.t: Water leaking into the trunk and damaging the audio amplifier
issues.sym: Water in the trunk, a radio that stops working, and climate controls that will not respond.
issues.why: Water can get into the trunk where the audio amplifier sits. Once the amplifier or nearby modules get wet, the radio and some controls can fail.
issues.next: Dry the trunk and have the leak found and sealed before the electronics are damaged further. Then have the wet modules tested and replaced if needed.

issues.t: Check engine light from a broken EVAP vapor line
issues.sym: Check engine light on, sometimes with a faint fuel smell.
issues.why: A line in the evaporative emissions (EVAP) system, which captures fuel vapors from the tank, can crack or break.
issues.next: Have the codes read. If you smell raw fuel, don't drive it: park it outside, away from sparks, and have it checked before driving again.

issues.t: Brake grinding or rattling noises and poor brake feel
issues.sym: Rattling or metal-on-metal grinding from the brakes, or brakes that feel weak or inconsistent.
issues.why: Brake complaints show up across the later CT6 years. Worn pads, rusted rotors and loose hardware are common causes on a heavy car like this.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected soon. Grinding usually means the pads are worn to metal, which also ruins the rotors.

issues.t: Super Cruise will not engage or keeps shutting off
issues.sym: The hands-free Super Cruise system stays unavailable or drops out on roads where it should work.
issues.why: Super Cruise needs its driver-facing camera, map data, GPS and the OnStar connection all working together. A fault or out-of-date data in any of them can disable it.
issues.next: Make sure the map and software updates are installed and that OnStar is active. If it still will not work, a dealer can check the camera and modules.

issues.t: Rattles and odd noises inside the cabin
issues.sym: Buzzing, rattling or other strange sounds from inside the car or from underneath while driving.
issues.why: Owners of early CT6 cars report interior and driveline noises, including a buzzing sound from near the transmission oil pan.
issues.next: Note when the noise happens (speed, bumps, temperature) and have a dealer ride along to find it. Loose trim and heat shields are common, simple fixes.

issues.t: A/C does not cool when the car is remote started
issues.sym: After a remote start, the cabin does not cool down as expected.
issues.why: On early CT6 cars, the climate system may not switch to cooling during a remote start, which is a settings or software issue rather than a failed A/C part.
issues.next: Check the remote start climate settings first, then ask a dealer whether a software update applies.
